title: Pessary for uterine prolapse
what: The doctor chooses and places a soft silicone ring in the vagina. It supports the uterus and the vaginal walls.
why: For a dropped uterus or vaginal walls, when surgery is not needed yet or not wanted.
duration: fitting and placing it usually takes 15 to 30 minutes
tell_doctor: Your symptoms: heaviness, bulging, leaking urine
If you have discharge or bleeding
If you will remove the ring yourself

prepare.title: Bladder
prepare.text: Use the toilet before the visit.

prepare.title: Hygiene
prepare.text: In the morning, wash with warm water.

prepare.title: Clothes
prepare.text: Wear comfortable clothes and bring a pad.

steps: You lie on the exam chair
The doctor examines you and checks the prolapse
The right ring size is chosen
The ring is gently put in
You are asked to stand up, walk, and cough
The doctor checks that the ring stays in and does not bother you
The doctor explains how to care for it and when to come back
feel: While it is placed, you feel pressure, and it is unpleasant
A well-fitted ring is usually barely felt
after: Come for checks as scheduled. The ring is removed, cleaned, and the area is checked
If the doctor taught you, you can remove and clean it yourself
Sometimes a vaginal cream is prescribed
The ring is replaced with a new one on time. Your doctor will tell you when
red_flags: The ring fell out or presses hard
Pain, bleeding, or discharge with a bad smell
You cannot pee or have a bowel movement

faq.q: Can I live a normal life with a ring?
faq.a: Usually yes: walk, work, and exercise, but without heavy lifting.

faq.q: Can I have sex with the ring in?
faq.a: It depends on the type of ring. Ask your doctor.

reminders.text: Pessary fitting tomorrow. Bring a pad and your ID.
